mainTopic: How the משנה's rules about a confirmed זב are read (ספיקו טמא, 'his semen is impure'), and the closing משנה proving that שמואל הנביא was a נזיר.
overview: The גמרא explains two phrases in the משנה about a זב. רבא says ספיקו טמא is about a discharge that surely happened, where the only doubt is whether it was semen or זיבה. Since the man is already a confirmed זב, that doubt is impure. For 'his semen is impure', the גמרא first suggests that a זב's semen makes impure even by carrying (משא). רבי יהושע's ברייתא does not support this, so רב אדא בר אהבה reads the phrase as אין תולין בה: we don't blame a זב's discharge on a recent emission of semen. רב פפא explains that this is because the זב is weak. רבא challenges him from a new convert, and רב פפא answers that converting is the greatest weakness of all. The גמרא then revives the carrying reading as a dispute of תנאים: 24 hours or only that day. It bases each view on a different word in the פסוקים that שמואל contrasted. The last משנה of the מסכת teaches, following רבי נהוראי, that שמואל הנביא was a נזיר, learned from the word מורה. It also records רבי יוסי's objection and רבי נהוראי's reply. The גמרא then begins with רב's words to his son חייא, which continue on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא defines the doubt in 'his doubtful case is impure'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that ספיקו טמא is not about whether a discharge happened. A discharge surely happened, and the doubt is whether it was semen or זיבה. Since the man is already a confirmed זב, the doubt is ruled impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Don't say the doubt is whether he saw a discharge or didn't see one. Rather, he surely saw a discharge. The doubt is whether it came from semen or whether it was a sighting of זיבה. Since he is already established as impure, his doubtful case is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains what kind of doubt the משנה means when it says ספיקו טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we didn't even know that something came out, we would have no reason to call him impure. But here something certainly came out, and the only question is what kind of discharge it was. Because this man is already a confirmed זב (נזקק לטומאה), we lean toward impurity in this doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt; an uncertain case
He saw (here: he had a discharge)
A 'sighting,' meaning a discharge of זיבה
Has already become established as impure
His doubtful case is impure

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read ספיקו טמא as 'whenever we aren't sure anything happened, he is impure.' רבא limits it to a case where a discharge surely happened and only its type is unclear.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא תֵּימָא סָפֵק חֲזָא סָפֵק לָא חֲזָא.
phrases.english: Do not say it is doubtful whether he saw, doubtful whether he did not see.
phrases.notes: 'Saw' here means he had a discharge.

phrases.english: Rather, he certainly saw a discharge,
and it is doubtful whether it was because of semen,
or doubtful whether it was because of a sighting of zivah.
Since he has already been established as impure,
his doubtful case is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא: לא תימא ספק חזא ספק לא חזא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה's phrase ספיקו טמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doubt in ספיקו טמא is about the type of discharge (semen or זיבה), not about whether a discharge happened. Since the man is already a confirmed זב, the doubt is impure.

steps.title: What does 'his semen is impure' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה and asks what kind of impurity it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His semen is impure.' For what purpose?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the משנה and asks what 'his semen is impure' is meant to teach. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every man's semen is already impure. So the גמרא wants to know what new rule the משנה is teaching about the semen of a זב in particular.

keyTerms.meaning: Semen
For what? What does it come to teach?

phrases.english: 'His semen is impure.'
For what purpose?

steps.triggerLanguage: שכבת זרעו טמאה. למאי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of impurity does the משנה mean when it calls a זב's semen impure?

steps.title: It can't mean impurity by touch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the משנה means impurity by touch (מגע). Even a pure man's semen makes impure by touch, so that would teach nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means impurity by touching, is it any worse than the semen of a pure man?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible meaning, impurity by touch, and immediately rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every man's semen already makes impure by touch. A זב's semen is certainly no less impure than that, so the משנה would not need to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: Touching; impurity passed on by contact
Is it any worse? (meaning: of course it is at least as strong)
A pure person; here, a man who is not a זב

phrases.english: If you say it means impurity by touching,
is it any worse than the semen of a pure man?

steps.triggerLanguage: אילימא למגע — מי גרע משכבת זרע דטהור?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries a first answer to the question in step 2 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the משנה as talking about impurity by touch.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading would make the משנה teach nothing new, since all semen makes impure by touch.

steps.title: Suggestion: a זב's semen makes impure by carrying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה means that a זב's semen makes impure even by carrying (משא), just like זיבה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the semen of a זב makes impure by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new answer: the משנה is teaching that a זב's semen makes a person impure by carrying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular semen makes impure only by touch, not by carrying. Saying a זב's semen also makes impure by carrying would be a real new rule, so the משנה would have a reason to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying; impurity passed on by lifting or carrying something, even without touching it
A man who has had a זיבה discharge

phrases.english: Rather, the semen of a zav
makes impure by carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא זרעו של זב מטמא במשא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after the first one was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה means that a זב's semen makes impure by carrying.

steps.title: Who holds that a זב's semen makes impure by carrying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion by asking which תנא holds this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who have you heard that says the semen of a זב makes impure by carrying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer from step 4 by asking for a source. This sets up a search for a תנא who holds this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any reading of the משנה has to fit some known opinion. If no תנא says that a זב's semen makes impure by carrying, the answer in step 4 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Who have you heard say this? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: Who have you heard that says

phrases.aramaic: שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע שֶׁל זָב מְטַמֵּא בְּמַשָּׂא?
phrases.english: that the semen of a zav makes impure by carrying?

steps.triggerLanguage: מאן שמעת להא דאמר שכבת זרע של זב מטמא במשא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that a זב's semen makes impure by carrying.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A reading of the משנה needs a known תנא who holds that view.

steps.title: Possible source: רבי יהושע in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a ברייתא as the source. There רבי אליעזר says a זב's semen does not make impure by carrying, and רבי יהושע says it does, because it always contains tiny drops of זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is this תנא, as it was taught: רבי אליעזר says the semen of a זב does not make impure by carrying. רבי יהושע says it does make impure by carrying, because it cannot be without tiny drops of זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a possible source for the view in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע does say that a זב's semen makes impure by carrying. But notice his reason: the semen always has drops of זיבה mixed in. That reason is what the next step will focus on.

keyTerms.meaning: Tiny drops of זיבה
It is impossible

phrases.english: If you say it is this tanna, as it was taught:
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁכְבַת זַרְעוֹ שֶׁל זָב אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא בְּמַשָּׂא,
phrases.english: the semen of a zav does not make impure by carrying,
and Rabbi Yehoshua says: it makes impure by carrying,
because it is impossible for it to be
without tiny drops of zivah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אילימא האי תנא, דתניא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible source in answer to the challenge in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The view that a זב's semen makes impure by carrying.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's opinion in the ברייתא.

steps.title: Even רבי יהושע doesn't mean the semen itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי יהושע only says the semen makes impure by carrying because of the drops of זיבה in it, not because of the semen itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even רבי יהושע only said this because of the tiny drops of זיבה. But about the semen by itself, he did not say it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא does not really support the reading from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהושע's view, the impurity by carrying comes from the זיבה mixed into the semen. The semen by itself does not make impure by carrying. So this ברייתא gives no source for the reading in step 4, and the גמרא turns to a different explanation. Step 12 later finds other תנאים who do hold it.

keyTerms.meaning: By itself; on its own, with nothing mixed in
Even

phrases.english: Even Rabbi Yehoshua did not say it
except because of the tiny drops of zivah,
but about it by itself, he did not say it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אפילו רבי יהושע לא אמר אלא משום ציחצוחי זיבה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the ברייתא as a source, which knocks out the reading in step 4.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהושע's impurity comes from the זיבה mixed in, not from the semen itself.

steps.title: New reading: we don't blame the discharge on the semen
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that 'his semen is impure' means we do not blame a later discharge on the semen (אין תולין בה). For a confirmed זב, the discharge counts as זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אדא בר אהבה said: it comes to say that we do not attribute the discharge to it.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the carrying reading failed, רב אדא בר אהבה gives a completely new meaning to the משנה's phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not adding a new kind of impurity to the semen. It is telling us that a man who is already a זב cannot say a discharge came only because he had just emitted semen. The discharge still counts as זיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: We attribute; we blame a result on a certain cause
It comes to say; it is teaching

steps.whatToRemember: רב אדא בר אהבה reads 'his semen is impure' as אין תולין בה: once a man is a confirmed זב, we don't blame his discharge on a recent emission of semen. Step 12 shows that the carrying reading is still possible, as a dispute of תנאים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא re-reads a משנה when the simple reading seems to have no תנא to support it. Here the phrase is read as a rule about how to count discharges instead of a rule about impurity by carrying, though step 12 later revives the carrying reading as a dispute between תנאים.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
It comes to say that we do not attribute it to the semen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אמר רב אדא בר אהבה: לומר שאין תולין בה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected carrying reading with a new meaning of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the meaning of the משנה's words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'His semen is impure' means a זב's semen makes impure by carrying.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means we do not blame a discharge on the semen, so for a confirmed זב it counts as זיבה.

steps.title: רב פפא's reason: the זב is weak
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests that we don't blame a later discharge on the semen because the זב is already weak from his זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In front of רבא, רב פפא wanted to say: the reason is that he sees the discharge because of weakness.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a reason for רב אדא בר אהבה's rule that we don't blame a later discharge on the semen (אין תולין).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A confirmed זב is already weakened by his earlier זיבה. So a later discharge is most likely more זיבה caused by that weakness, and not a side effect of the semen. That is why it counts as זיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of רבא (while learning before him)
Weakness
Because of, due to

phrases.aramaic: סְבַר רַב פָּפָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא לְמֵימַר
phrases.english: Rav Pappa thought, in front of Rava, to say:
It is because of weakness that he sees the discharge.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבַר רַב פָּפָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a reason for רב אדא בר אהבה's explanation in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זב's later discharge is treated as זיבה because his earlier זיבה left him weak.

steps.title: רבא's challenge from a new convert
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges: a new convert becomes a זב right away, even though he has no earlier weakness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But we learned in a משנה that a convert who just converted can become impure through זיבה immediately!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב פפא's reason by quoting a משנה about a new convert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new convert never had זיבה, so he has no 'weakness' from it. Even so, his discharge is not blamed on semen he had before converting, and it counts as זיבה. That suggests weakness is not the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert who has just converted
Immediately

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
A convert who has just converted
becomes impure immediately through ziva!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא, וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's reason from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that weakness is the reason we don't blame the discharge on semen.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A new convert has no weakness from earlier זיבה, yet the same rule applies to him.

steps.title: Converting is itself a great illness
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that becoming a convert is the greatest 'illness' of all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You have no illness greater than this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends his reason: the convert is also 'weak.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking on the full burden of the מצוות is so heavy that it counts as a kind of weakness. So the convert fits the weakness reason too, and רב פפא's explanation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Illness
You have no... (nothing is more than...)

phrases.english: He said to him:
You have no illness greater than this.
phrases.notes: He means taking on the burden of the מצוות is so heavy that it counts as a weakness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין לְךָ חוֹלִי גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case so it fits the rule: conversion counts as weakness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A convert has no weakness, so the weakness reason fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: Converting is itself a great weakness, so the reason still works.

steps.title: Back to carrying: it is a dispute of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the reading that a זב's semen makes impure by carrying, and finds תנאים who hold this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a dispute between תנאים. As a ברייתא teaches: a זב's semen makes impure by carrying for a full 24 hours. רבי יוסי says: only on its day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now answers step 5's question, 'Which תנא holds this?', with a different ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 pushed away the proof from רבי יהושע. Now the גמרא finds a ברייתא where both תנאים agree that a זב's semen itself makes impure by carrying. They only argue about how long this lasts: 24 hours, or only until the end of that day.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
A full 24-hour period
Its day (only until that night)

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions here agree that the semen makes impure by carrying. They only argue about how long. This is different from the ברייתא in step 6, where רבי אליעזר said it does not make impure by carrying at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the reading from step 4: the משנה can follow these תנאים.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a dispute of tannaim.
phrases.notes: The גמרא goes back to the idea from step 4, that a זב's semen makes impure by carrying.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
The semen of a zav
makes impure by carrying
for a full twenty-four hour period.
phrases.notes: Meaning, if the semen came within 24 hours of his זיבה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei says: only its day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, תַּנָּאֵי הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רב אדא's explanation and goes back to answer step 5's question about the reading from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a different source for the opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No תנא clearly holds that a זב's semen itself makes impure by carrying.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא and רבי יוסי both hold it does; they only argue about how long.

steps.title: What is their dispute based on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason is behind the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking for the source behind the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the semen makes impure by carrying. The גמרא wants to know why one says 24 hours and the other says only that day.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the dispute in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source behind the 24-hour view and the 'its day' view.

steps.title: שמואל's contradiction between two verses
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is about שמואל's contradiction: one פסוק speaks of 'night,' the next speaks of 'evening turning.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about what שמואל raised. שמואל pointed out a contradiction: it is written, 'If there is among you a man who is not pure because of what happens at night,' and it is written, 'When evening turns, he shall bathe in water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the dispute goes back to two פסוקים that שמואל compared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These פסוקים are about a זב who had a discharge of semen. One פסוק mentions 'night,' and the next mentions 'when evening turns.' Each תנא builds his time limit on a different one of these words.

keyTerms.meaning: Points out a contradiction
Because of what happens at night
When evening turns

phrases.english: About the issue of Shmuel.
For Shmuel pointed out a contradiction:
It is written: "If there is among you a man

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִהְיֶה טָהוֹר מִקְּרֵה לָיְלָה״.
phrases.english: who is not pure because of what happens at night."
And it is written: "When evening turns, he shall bathe in water."

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּדִשְׁמוּאֵל. דִּשְׁמוּאֵל רָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute depends on שמואל's contradiction between 'night' and 'when evening turns.'

steps.title: Each תנא learns from a different word
steps.stepSummary: The 24-hour view learns from 'when evening turns'; רבי יוסי learns from 'what happens at night.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 24 hours learns it from 'when evening turns,' and the other learns it from 'what happens at night.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes by showing which פסוק each side uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא reads 'when evening turns' as reaching to the next evening, so the impurity of carrying lasts a full 24 hours. רבי יוסי reads 'what happens at night' as stopping at that night, so it lasts only until the end of that day.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says
Learns it from a careful reading
The other one

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא and רבי יוסי agree a זב's semen makes impure by carrying. The תנא קמא says 24 hours (from 'when evening turns'); רבי יוסי says only that day (from 'what happens at night').

phrases.english: The one who says a twenty-four hour period
learns it from "when evening turns,"
phrases.notes: He reads 'turns' as reaching to the next evening, so a full day and night.

phrases.english: and the other learns it from "what happens at night."
phrases.notes: So for him it lasts only until that night, the end of the same day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מֵעֵת לְעֵת דָּיֵיק מִ״לִּפְנוֹת עֶרֶב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how each side of step 12 uses one of the פסוקים from step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The 24-hour view comes from 'when evening turns'; רבי יוסי's 'its day' view comes from 'what happens at night.'

steps.title: Challenge to the view that learns from 'when evening turns'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that learns from 'לפנות ערב': the תורה also says 'מקרה לילה,' which sounds like it limits the rule to night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who learns the law from 'when evening turns' has a problem, because the פסוק also says 'an occurrence of night'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the other side of the argument. It asks how the 24-hour view deals with the words 'מקרה לילה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 15 we saw that one view learns from 'לפנות ערב' and רבי יוסי learns from 'מקרה לילה.' Now the גמרא asks the first view: if you ignore the word 'night,' why did the תורה write it? That word seems to support רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'An occurrence of night,' meaning an emission at night (דברים 23:11)
'When evening turns' (דברים 23:12)
'But it is written!', a formula used to bring a challenge from a פסוק

phrases.english: And the one who says [it is learned] from "when evening turns,"
phrases.notes: This is the 24-hour view from Step 15.

phrases.english: but it is written "an occurrence of night"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר מִ״לִּפְנוֹת עֶרֶב״, הָכְתִיב ״מִקְּרֵה לָיְלָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 24-hour side of the explanation given in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that learns the rule from 'לפנות ערב'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק explicitly says 'night,' which suggests the rule depends on night and is not a 24-hour period.

steps.title: The פסוק just describes the usual case
steps.stepSummary: The 24-hour view answers that the תורה wrote 'night' only because emissions usually happen at night. The word does not set a legal limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would answer you: the normal way an emission happens is at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the 24-hour view. The word 'night' is just describing what usually happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a classic move: the תורה speaks about the common situation (דיבר הכתוב בהווה). So you cannot learn a strict rule from the word 'night.' The real rule comes from 'לפנות ערב.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'He would say to you,' introducing how a view would defend itself
The usual way, the normal manner
A seminal emission

steps.whatToRemember: Both views now have an explanation. רבי יוסי reads 'מקרה לילה' strictly. The 24-hour view says 'night' is just the usual case and learns its rule from 'לפנות ערב.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common tool in the גמרא: a word in a פסוק may describe the typical case without limiting the law to it.

phrases.english: He would say to you,
the usual way of an emission is to come at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ, אוֹרְחָא דְקֶרִי לֵמֵתֵיא בְּלֵילְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק speaks about the usual case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'night' limits the law to emissions at night.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Night' just describes when emissions usually happen. The rule itself is learned from 'לפנות ערב.'

steps.title: שמואל was a נזיר, learned from שמשון
steps.stepSummary: The final משנה of the מסכת teaches, following רבי נהוראי, that שמואל was a נזיר. This is learned through a גזירה שוה on the word 'מורה' used for both שמשון and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: שמואל was a נזיר, according to רבי נהוראי. חנה said, 'And no מורה shall come upon his head.' The word מורה is used for שמשון and also for שמואל. Just as by שמשון it means he was a נזיר, so by שמואל it means he was a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, the last one in the מסכת. רבי נהוראי proves that שמואל הנביא was a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By שמשון, the פסוק says no מורה (razor) will come on his head, 'for the child will be a נזיר.' So there 'מורה' clearly means a razor and is tied to נזירות. Since חנה used the same word for שמואל, the גזירה שוה teaches that שמואל was a נזיר too.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
A razor. רבי יוסי will argue that it means fear
A person who may not cut his hair, drink wine or become טמא from a dead body
Learning from the same word used in two places

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Shmuel was a nazir,
phrases.notes: This is שמואל the prophet, not the אמורא שמואל from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: according to the words of Rabbi Nehorai,
as it says: "and no mora shall come upon his head."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:11, from חנה's prayer for a son.

phrases.english: It says regarding Shimshon "and mora,"
and it says regarding Shmuel "and mora."
Just as the "mora" stated about Shimshon [means] a nazir,
so too the "mora" stated about Shmuel [means] a nazir.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נָזִיר הָיָה שְׁמוּאֵל, כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins. It is not related to the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל הנביא was a נזיר. This is learned through a גזירה שוה of 'מורה' from שמשון.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: מורה means fear of people
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי challenges the proof. He says 'מורה' means fear of a human being, not a razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: But doesn't 'מורה' mean only fear of flesh and blood?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי attacks רבי נהוראי's proof. He reads חנה's words in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי reads מורה as if it were מורא, 'fear.' Then חנה was praying that her son would never fear any human. If so, the word has nothing to do with a razor, and the גזירה שוה from שמשון falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But isn't it so...?', introducing a challenge
Flesh and blood, meaning a human being
Fear

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up מורה (with a ה, razor) and מורא (with an א, fear). The whole argument turns on which meaning חנה intended.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
But doesn't "mora" mean nothing
other than [fear] of flesh and blood!
phrases.notes: He reads the word like מורא, fear. So חנה was asking that her son would never be afraid of any person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וַהֲלֹא אֵין מוֹרָה אֶלָּא שֶׁל בָּשָׂר וָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of 'מורה' that the proof in Step 18 depends on.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If מורה means 'fear,' it is not the same word as שמשון's 'razor,' so there is no basis to compare them.

steps.title: רבי נהוראי: שמואל did fear שאול
steps.stepSummary: רבי נהוראי answers that שמואל clearly feared שאול. So 'מורה' cannot mean 'no fear of people.' It must mean a razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נהוראי said to him: But it already says, 'And שמואל said: How can I go? If שאול hears, he will kill me.' So שמואל already had fear of a human being.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נהוראי defends his proof. He shows a פסוק where שמואל is afraid of שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חנה had meant 'my son will never fear any person,' that would not fit the story, because שמואל did fear שאול. So רבי יוסי's reading doesn't work. מורה must mean a razor, as by שמשון, and the proof that שמואל was a נזיר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The first king of ישראל, whom שמואל feared
'And he will kill me'

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with רבי נהוראי's view standing: שמואל was a נזיר. 'מורה' means a razor, because the 'fear' reading is disproved by שמואל's fear of שאול.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nehorai said to him:
But hasn't it already been said:
"And Shmuel said: How can I go,
if Shaul hears, he will kill me,"
[showing] that there already was upon him
fear of flesh and blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי's challenge from Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disproves the other reading using another פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מורה means 'fear,' so חנה was praying that שמואל would never fear people.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל did fear שאול, so מורה must mean 'razor,' and שמואל was a נזיר.

steps.title: The גמרא opens with רב's words to his son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא on the final משנה begins by introducing a teaching that רב told his son חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב said to his son חייא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is introducing something רב told his son, and the content comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening attribution appears here. What רב actually said continues right after this line, so we wait for it before analyzing.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
His son

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav said to his son Chiya:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְחִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the final משנה. This line sets up a teaching that continues in the next section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduction only. רב's teaching to חייא follows.
